scope: Offline preliminary comparison. No Fusion, no edits to preliminary/, pan/ or chassis/.
asymmetry: A's custody and delivery come from a spatial 12-case field replay with peers, clock, current limit and finite panels. B-D come from planar screens (impulse disc against the trough section) and bottom-up estimates. A's figures are deeper evidence than B's; B's advantages are predictions to be confirmed by the bench gate below, not equal-basis results.

role.mission: Two TELEOP trips (match s 18-153): receive one station-issued CORAL (4.5 in OD x 11.875 in pipe, 0.816 kg upper bound) at the station face, carry it, place it in red L1 trough sector A then B, keep it credited, observe the score and return to a ready, serviceable state.
requirements: R1 receive: accept a pipe arriving at up to 2.47 m/s (adverse admission) rolling axis-across from the station
R2 carry: keep custody through route accelerations, 3-8 g peer pulses and bumper strikes
R3 deliver: leave the pipe supported in the low trough (lip top 457.2 mm, 15 deg floor, riser 518 mm) over the real dock scatter
R4 reset: ready for the next receive within the trip clock
R5 fit: R103 mass, R101-R104 perimeter and 42 in start height, R102/R105 18 in extension, weak-pack bus >= 9 V
R6 service: repair or swap at a pit in a typical student shop
role.throughput: Two pieces in 135 s. Mechanism time is not the discriminator; custody and delivery robustness are.

G412.statement: A launched CORAL requires a bumper partially in its own reef zone.
G412.reason: Record the actual release behavior and registered footprint.

notes: B launches the pipe (about 0.1 s airborne): G412 requires a bumper partially in our reef zone at release, so the eject command must be interlocked on reef-zone pose; the register marks G412 unmodeled.
B'x places by roll-off; whether a roll-off counts as launched under G412 is an open rules question. Its deployed lip and A's 179 mm dumped reach both fall under R102/R105 (18 in).
Stowed height 0.9405 m is under the registered 42 in (1.067 m) start height.

A.name: Guarded tipping pan (r3, current)
A.summary: Rotating 430 x 322 mm pan on a NEO 550 / 54.8:1 drive; receives at 70 deg stow against a spring-preloaded stop, tips to -2 deg so the pipe slides off over the trough.

B.name: Fixed pocket, two-roller nip, low-speed launch
B.summary: Fixed tray and inlet; the pipe settles in an enclosed pocket (centre 0.60 m) against a 70 mm fence leaning 20 deg toward the pocket, low-friction face on compliant backing, under a two-roller nip; one NEO 550 (12:1) lifts it over the fence and launches it at 1.3 m/s (closed loop) from 0.67 m, inside the frame perimeter.

B'0.name: B pocket and nip, roll-off from the frame edge (KitBot-style placement)
B'0.summary: As B, then a short down-sloping exit lip rolls the pipe off the frame edge at low speed.

B'x.name: B pocket and nip, roll-off from a 100 mm one-time-deployed exit lip
B'x.summary: As B'0, but a polycarbonate exit lip deploys once at match start so the pipe leaves 100 mm beyond the frame perimeter, above the trough lip, at 0.55 m and 0.6-1.5 m/s.

C.name: Fixed pocket with a passive reef-tripped gate
C.summary: Same pocket; a spring gate is released by a plunger touching the reef; gravity roll-out.

D.name: Pivoting roller end effector
D.summary: Short arm with an intake/eject roller pair that receives at the station and swings over the trough.

fixedPathFairness.tested: Pan geometry frozen at the -8 deg dump pose: 14 mm front lip, optional 8 mm notch bump, passive brush damping, no actuator. Release only by a scripted 9 m/s^2 chassis stop.
fixedPathFairness.verdict: Not a fair test of a fixed-geometry receiver. The arrival carries about 42x the energy needed to roll over the 14 mm lip, so the undamped variant and the lightly damped c6 and c10 lost the pipe at receive in 12 of 12 cases. The damped notch variants c15 and c22 and the floor-brush variants c10, c15 and c22 lost it in adverse carry in 6 of 12 cases each (notch c15 lost the other 6 parked before release; floor-brush c10 lost all 12 in carry). In the remaining cases notch c22 and floor-brush c15 and c22 kept the pipe but could not release it, because no variant had a release actuator. The test rejects a zero-actuator frozen pan. It does not test a fixed pocket with a closed exit and a powered release. The FIRST 2025 KitBot citation supports only the role (a Coral Station-fed Level 1 scorer), not any exit mechanism.

requirements.finding: 12:1 gives 2.44 m/s free at 12 V and 2.09 m/s at 10.3 V. B needs 1.1-1.5 m/s (+/-15 %); fixed duty alone spreads about +/-11 % from 10 to 12.5 V before slip and load, so B needs closed-loop roller velocity on the NEO 550 encoder (target 1.3 m/s, tolerance +/-5 %) and an eject interlock below 9.5 V; headroom at 10 V is 1.6x. B'x (0.6-1.5 m/s, +/-43 %) tolerates open-loop duty.

recommendation.select: B family (fixed pocket + nip), exit chosen at the bench: B'x if the deployed lip passes, else B
recommendation.confidence: about 55 % that the B family meets the role better than A; low-medium that it passes the bench gate first time
recommendation.doNotDiscard: Do NOT discard or stop maintaining the r3 pan package until bench gates G1-G4 pass. If they fail, A remains the selected architecture and the r3 fixes continue.
recommendation.invalidatesIfGatesPass: Most of the r3 pan package: moving pan, drive, clutch, cam and switch, spring, stow and soft stops, root-moment joint, plate-stack posts and bulkhead; the C2/C3/P3/titanium mass work becomes unnecessary.

mostConsequentialUntested.A: unpowered custody fails at >= 3 g opening contact; the selected K5420 support margin is +1.9 um over its own criterion (-3.2 um unpowered, pan-stop-study-05 findings)

benchGate.article: Real B pocket: 70 mm fence leaning 20 deg toward the pocket, UHMW or polycarbonate face on 25 mm compliant backing, 10 mm hood, 200 mm pocket with spring check flap, two-roller nip (2 in 35A compliant wheels, 12 mm compression), NEO 550 12:1 with closed-loop velocity; for B'x add the deployed lip with the pipe leaving 100 mm beyond the frame line at 0.55 m. Real 4.5 in PVC pipes at 0.82 kg (new and worn). Trough mock per target.json: lip top 457.2 mm, lip 12.7 mm, 15 deg floor, riser top 517.5 mm at 248 mm.
benchGate.G1 receive: Feed 30 pipes rolling axis-across at 2.85 +/- 0.10 m/s (measured by light gates or 240 fps video), nip stalled in brake: PASS 30/30 seated within 0.5 s, 0 rises above 10 mm at the fence, 0 entries into the nip, 0 rearward escapes past the flap; repeat 10 with the controller unpowered: 10/10. KILL on any climb over the fence.
benchGate.G2 eject into trough: Stand-offs 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 mm x bus 10.0, 11.0, 12.0 V (loaded, measured) x 10 ejects = 150 per exit variant, target 1.3 m/s (B) or 1.0 m/s (B'x): PASS >= 147/150 captured and still supported 2 s later, every cell >= 9/10, measured pipe exit speed inside 1.1-1.5 m/s (B) in 150/150. KILL the variant if any cell is <= 7/10.
benchGate.G3 custody sled: Pocket loaded, nip unpowered, 1, 3 and 8 g / 50 ms pulses forward and rearward, 10 each: PASS 60/60 retained in the pocket. KILL on any loss at <= 3 g.
benchGate.G4 end to end: 20 consecutive cycles: G1 feed, 5 m carry with 1.5 m/s^2 braking, G2 eject at a random stand-off 0-100 mm and random 10-12 V: PASS >= 19/20 credited with no hand recovery.
benchGate.decision: All of G1-G4 pass -> retire r3 and start B-family Fusion. G1 or G3 fails -> retain A. G2 fails for B but passes for B'x -> select B'x after an R105/G412 ruling. Then run the fair spatial 12-case replay with a pocket-and-nip element before shop release.
